flaws.title: Refill throws away partial progress
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to refill the bucket, how to track the last refill time, or how to compute tokens from elapsed time.
flaws.wrongClaim: Compute whole tokens from elapsed time and then set the bucket's last timestamp to now() on every call, calling that simple and correct.
flaws.correctBehavior: Advance the timestamp only by the whole intervals that were credited (last += n * refillEveryMs), so leftover time carries over. Setting it to now() loses progress, especially on denied calls.

flaws.title: Denied requests still spend tokens
flaws.trigger: The learner asks for tryConsume, or how to deny a request when the bucket is short.
flaws.wrongClaim: Subtract cost first, then decide with `allowed = tokens >= 0`, presenting it as a simpler way to write tryConsume.
flaws.correctBehavior: A denied call must leave the bucket unchanged. Check tokens >= cost first and only then subtract.

flaws.title: retryAfterMs ignores time already waited
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to compute retryAfterMs, or how long a client should wait.
flaws.correctBehavior: Subtract the time already elapsed toward the next token: (cost - tokens) * refillEveryMs - (now - last).

flaws.title: Assumes Date.now() never goes backwards
flaws.trigger: The learner asks about time handling, the injected clock, or what to do if elapsed time is odd.
flaws.wrongClaim: State that Date.now() is monotonic, so no guard for time going backwards is needed, and compute elapsed as `now - last` directly.
flaws.correctBehavior: Date.now() follows the wall clock and can jump backwards (NTP or manual changes). Guard against negative elapsed time, and re-base the timestamp. performance.now() is the monotonic one.

flaws.title: prune() deletes by idle time, not by fullness
flaws.trigger: The learner asks about memory growth, cleanup, or how to implement prune().
flaws.wrongClaim: Delete every bucket whose last timestamp is older than refillEveryMs, on the grounds that idle keys are safe to forget.
flaws.correctBehavior: Only delete buckets that are full after refill. A partially refilled bucket that is deleted comes back full, which lets a throttled client bypass the limit.

flaws.title: Full bucket keeps a stale remainder
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to cap tokens at capacity, or asks for the refill function.
flaws.wrongClaim: Cap with `tokens = Math.min(capacity, tokens + n)` and advance `last += n * refillEveryMs`, with no special handling once the bucket is full.
flaws.correctBehavior: When the bucket reaches capacity, set last = now(), because a full bucket has no partial progress. Otherwise time spent while full is credited as head start on the next token.
